title: The Division Rule: Repeated Letters and Round Tables
short: Divide out the orderings that look the same: MISSISSIPPI has 11!/(4! · 4! · 2!) arrangements, and n people around a round table have (n − 1)!.
trouble: Students divide by the wrong factorials, or count rotations of the same seating at a round table as different.

blocks.html: The product rule counts arrangements as if every item were different, which is how permutations work. When some arrangements look the same (repeated letters, seats around a round table), the product rule overcounts. If the overcount is the same for every object, one division fixes it.

Division rule: if a method produces every object exactly $d$ times, the number of objects is (the method's count) $\div\ d$. Arrangements of $n$ letters with one letter repeated $k_{1}$ times, another $k_{2}$ times, and so on: $\dfrac{n!}{k_{1}!\,k_{2}!\cdots}$. Seatings of $n$ people around a round table (rotations counted as the same): $(n - 1)!$.

Give the copies of each letter temporary labels, like $A_{1}A_{2}A_{3}$ in BANANA. Now all letters are different, and there are $6! = 720$ labeled arrangements. Erasing the labels merges arrangements that differ only in how the copies are labeled: $3!$ orders of the A's times $2!$ orders of the N's, the same $12$ for every word. So there are $720 / 12 = 60$ words. For a round table, each seating appears $n$ times among the $n!$ row orders, once for each place where you could cut the circle.

blocks.cap: BANANA with labeled copies: every word appears as $3! \cdot 2! = 12$ labeled arrangements.

blocks.title: A long word
blocks.q: How many arrangements of MISSISSIPPI are there?
steps: $11$ letters: M once, I four times, S four times, P twice.
Labeled arrangements: $11!$. Each word appears $4! \cdot 4! \cdot 2!$ times.

blocks.title: A round table
blocks.q: In how many ways can $6$ people sit around a round table, if seatings that are rotations of each other count as the same?
steps: Each round seating is counted $6$ times, once for each rotation.
$720 / 6 = 120 = 5!$. Equivalently: seat one person anywhere, then arrange the other $5$ relative to them.

blocks.title: Rotations and flips
blocks.q: How many different bracelets can be made from $5$ different beads, if a bracelet can be rotated or flipped over?
steps: Around a circle, up to rotation: $(5 - 1)! = 24$.
Flipping turns each arrangement into its mirror image. For $5$ different beads, an arrangement never matches its own mirror image, so each bracelet was counted twice.

blocks.html: Dividing by the wrong factorials, or not dividing for rotations. For BANANA, dividing by $3!$ alone (for the A's) forgets the N's; dividing by $6!/2$ or by $2!$ for each letter makes no sense. And at a round table, $6!$ counts rotations as different seatings. Check: divide by one factorial for each repeated letter, using that letter's count; and ask whether two outcomes your method separates would look identical.
